description: Maven : outil de gestion de projet Java — pom.xml, dépendances, repositories, scopes, plugins, commandes de build et différence avec Gradle.

questions.prompt: What is Maven and what is it used for?
questions.answer_text:
Maven is a Java project management tool. Using the pom.xml, it manages dependencies, compilation, testing, and packaging. It is used to:
- Manage dependencies (external libraries).
- Automate compilation, testing, and packaging.
- Standardize project structure with the pom.xml.

Example: with `mvn clean install`, you clean, compile, test, and install the project into the local repository in a single command.

questions.prompt: What are the important Maven commands?
questions.answer_text:
- mvn clean : deletes the target folder (old compiled files: .class, .jar). Use before recompiling for a clean project.
- mvn compile : compiles Java source (src/main/java). To check the code compiles.
- mvn test : runs unit tests (src/test/java).
- mvn package : compile + test + create a .jar/.war in target/.
- mvn install : installs the .jar/.war into the local repository (.m2) to reuse it as a dependency.
- mvn clean install : clean + compile + test + package + install into .m2 (the most commonly used, complete pipeline).
- mvn spring-boot:run : runs a Spring Boot application directly.

questions.prompt: What are the core Maven concepts (pom.xml, dependency, repository, plugin, scope)?
questions.answer_text:
- pom.xml : the main configuration file of a Maven project (contains dependencies, plugins, project info).
- Dependency : an external library automatically downloaded by Maven (e.g. Spring Boot, Hibernate, MySQL driver).
- Repository : where Maven looks for/downloads dependencies — Local (.m2), Central (Internet), Remote (private repo).
- Plugin : tools that extend Maven to perform tasks (maven-compiler-plugin to compile, spring-boot-maven-plugin to run Spring Boot).
- Scope : defines when a dependency is used (compile, provided, runtime, test).

questions.prompt: What is the difference between Maven and Gradle?
questions.answer_text:
Both are build tools.
- Maven uses an XML file (pom.xml) and is simpler to use — simplicity & convention.
- Gradle uses a DSL (Groovy/Kotlin), is more flexible, and faster thanks to incremental builds — flexibility & performance.

pom.xml stands for Project Object Model. It is the main configuration file of a Maven project. It contains:
- Dependencies
- Plugins
- Project information (name, version, packaging).

A dependency is an external library your project needs. Maven automatically downloads it from a repository and adds it to your project.

Example :
<dependency>
  <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
  <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-web</artifactId>
  <version>3.2.0</version>
</dependency>

questions.prompt: What are 'repositories' in Maven (local, central, remote)?
questions.answer_text:
A repository is where Maven stores or retrieves dependencies:
- Local repository → on your PC, in the .m2 folder.
- Central repository → the official online repository (default).
- Remote repository → a private company repository (e.g. Nexus, Artifactory).

questions.prompt: What is the difference between compile, provided, runtime, and test scopes in Maven?
questions.answer_text:
Scopes define when a dependency is used:
- compile (default) → used at compile time and runtime.
- provided → used at compile time but not packaged (e.g. servlet-api, provided by Tomcat).
- runtime → not needed at compile time, only at runtime (e.g. JDBC driver).
- test → used only for testing (e.g. JUnit).

questions.prompt: How does Maven handle transitive dependencies?
questions.answer_text: When you add one dependency (e.g. Spring Boot Starter Web), Maven also downloads all the libraries it depends on (e.g. Tomcat, Jackson). This is called transitive dependencies — you don't need to declare everything manually.

A Maven plugin is a tool that adds a specific task to the build. Examples:
- maven-compiler-plugin → compiles Java code.
- maven-surefire-plugin → runs tests.
- spring-boot-maven-plugin → runs a Spring Boot app.
Plugins are defined inside the pom.xml.

questions.prompt: How do you run a Maven build?
questions.answer_text:
You use Maven commands in the terminal:
- mvn clean → deletes old compiled files (target/).
- mvn compile → compiles the project.
- mvn package → creates a .jar or .war.
- mvn install → installs the package into the local repository (.m2).
- mvn test → runs the tests.

questions.prompt: What does the command 'mvn clean install' do?
questions.answer_text:
It runs two chained steps:
- clean → removes old compiled files in the target/ folder.
- install → compiles, tests, packages the project, then installs the artifact into the local repository (.m2).
Result: you get a .jar (or .war) ready to be reused as a dependency in another project.
